About the job

Turn AI research ideas into experiments that help shape Graphcore’s next generation of AI hardware.

As a Staff Research Scientist in Graphcore Research, you’ll help shape complex projects from hypothesis to evaluation. You can join the team in Bristol, London or Cambridge.

Our research spans efficient training and inference, numerics, reinforcement learning, and more. You’ll build implementations and algorithms that scale and explore how choices in model design and execution affect hardware efficiency.

Your work will help to push AI models past the frontier, while turning the results of your work into recommendations that silicon and software engineers can use in their designs. You will explain to various groups which trade-offs matter as models grow and where bottlenecks emerge.

You’ll also prepare papers and present findings at AI conferences and specialist workshops. 

The team and culture

Researchers across Bristol, London and Cambridge shape projects around shared research interests. You might work with colleagues to investigate how a model scales, trace a distributed inference bottleneck, or develop an algorithm that enables training with more efficient number formats. 

Research team bring a customer perspective and experience making models and software work on Graphcore’s stack at scale. Together, the teams develop ideas in efficient compute, model scaling and distributed training and inference.

Graphcore Research works with research groups around the world and publishes at venues including NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR.

What we’re looking for

• A PhD or equivalent experience in a technical discipline such as mathematics, statistics, computer science, physics or chemistry.

• Python skills with a framework such as PyTorch or JAX, with experience in model design, optimisation, evaluation and scaling.

• Ability to design, run and evaluate machine learning experiments and turn results into clear, actionable reports.

• Experience writing low-level code for hardware efficiency and reasoning about threads, caches, compute engines and memory bandwidth.

• Practical understanding of deep learning software stacks, including compilation, kernel fusion, framework operators, streams and asynchronous execution.

• A track record of providing technical leadership on complex work.

We also value applied skills in calculus, probability and linear algebra, or publications at leading AI conferences. Experience training frontier language models or training across large accelerator clusters is strongly desired.
